bodytext:
Andrea Brandstätter has been doing boundary work in this district since 2004 and joined Aubruck the year after. She runs the cadastral side of the office and looks after the control network — the seventy-odd fixed points the whole district measures against, which somebody has to check every spring whether or not anybody is paying for it.

Most of her week is spent on the small, unglamorous jobs: a garden wall that was built forty centimetres over a line nobody had looked at since 1963, a subdivision that has to be filed before a sale can close, a fence two neighbours have stopped speaking about. She has been to court four times in twenty-one years and considers each of them a failure of an earlier conversation.

She trained at the technical college in Sandau, spent three years at the cadastral office before moving to private practice, and has taken every apprentice this office has had out on their first boundary survey.
